summary: Baileys fork with co-occurring child_process and https.request primitives; no traced installer-harm path
details: zero-baileys@2.5.5 is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. A static pattern flagged lib/Utils/messages-media.js for co-occurrence of require("child_process"), an https.request call, and a POST verb across the same file (lines 28, 673-677). The Baileys library legitimately uses child_process to spawn ffmpeg for media transcoding and issues HTTPS POSTs against WhatsApp's own media endpoints, which produces the same primitive co-occurrence as an exfil shape. No traced code path shows installer-side secrets (env vars, ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser stores) being read and sent to a non-first-party destination, and no attacker-controlled hostname is bound to the POST in the cited evidence. As a fork of a widely used library, the possibility of an injected covert action using the consumer's WhatsApp session (such as auto-follow/subscribe patterns previously seen in Baileys forks) cannot be confirmed or ruled out from the co-occurrence pattern alone.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
